correctness.rationale: For a Haar (n-q)-plane E, normal-subspace frame Q=G(G^T G)^-1/2 yields leverage scores ell_i=||Q^T e_i||²=(1/n)g_i^T S_n^-1 g_i, with S_n=G^T G/n ->I for fixed q. Hence projected antipodal radius is sqrt(1-ell_i), and the nearest-sphere deficit scaled by n^{1+2/q} is asymptotically n^{2/q}||g_i||²/2. Since iid chi²_q have small-ball probability x^{q/2}/[2^{q/2}Γ(1+q/2)](1+O(x)), the original n marked-pair deficits form a PPP with cumulative intensity t^{q/2}/Γ(1+q/2). Wishart spectral concentration plus min-chi-square tail uniform integrability gives all positive moments of Y=min deficits: Γ(1+q/2)^{2p/q} Γ(1+2p/q), while Poisson counts give kth order survival law. In n=3,q=1, a unit sphere normal gives max radius sqrt(1-min|u_i|²); inclusion-exclusion on |u_i|<s gives the displayed exact arcsin/arctan CDF. Four independent quadrature checks reproduced the formula. Distinguish generating antipodal pairs from actual vertices of a projected polytope.
